title: Approve this week's expense claims - properly
context: Peter Walsh, Management Accountant, has been asked to clear the expense claims awaiting approval in Ledgerline before Friday's payment run. Each claim in the Expense Claims list has a receipt photo in Finance > Invoices > Claim Receipts (Ledgerline). Line managers have been approving on the claimed amount alone, without opening the receipts.
goal: Check every claim awaiting approval against its receipt and the Expenses Policy, and produce an approve / query / reject list with reasons.
task_steps: Open the Expense Claims list (or the Excel export) and filter to 'Awaiting approval'.
Ask Copilot to summarise the claims: count, total value, claims per approver.
For each claim, open the receipt image (or attach several to Copilot) and extract the total and line items.
Compare the receipt with the claimed amount, the category cap and the alcohol rule in the Expenses Policy.
Look for the same receipt claimed twice.
Produce a table: claim, claimant, decision (approve / query / reject part), reason, amount payable.
Draft a short, polite query message for each claimant who needs one.
sample_prompts: From the Expense Claims list, show me every claim awaiting approval with claimant, category, date and claimed amount.
Here are the receipts for these claims. For each one, give me the receipt total and any line items that are alcohol.
Using the Expenses Policy, which of these claims are over the meal cap, and what is the most we can pay?
Is any receipt here the same as a claim that has already been paid?
success_criteria: Every 'Awaiting approval' claim has a decision with a reason.
Claims where the claimed amount is more than the receipt are queried.
Alcohol and over-cap amounts are not paid; the payable amount is stated.
The duplicate claim is rejected and linked to the original paid claim.
Learner checked at least two of Copilot's receipt readings against the image.
trainer_notes: The list alone looks clean - the problems only show up on the receipts. Good discussion point: Copilot can read the list, but someone has to bring the images into the conversation. Watch for Copilot misreading totals on angled photos; insist learners spot-check.

title: Audit paid expenses and design an automated check
context: Priya Raman, CFO, has heard that some expense claims are being paid without anyone looking at the receipts. She wants to know how big the problem is, and a proposal for an automated first-pass check so it doesn't happen again.
goal: Find paid claims that broke policy, quantify the overpayment, and design a Copilot Studio agent or Power Automate flow that checks each new claim against its receipt and the policy before it reaches the approver.
task_steps: Use the Expense Claims data and receipts to find every paid claim that should not have been paid in full.
Calculate the overpayment per claim and in total.
Write a one-paragraph finding for the CFO.
Design the automated check: trigger, inputs (claim row + receipt image), rules from the Expenses Policy, outputs (flag, reason, suggested payable amount) and where a human must decide.
Build the agent (or flow) and test it against all 31 claims; compare its flags with your own audit.
sample_prompts: Which paid expense claims were for more than the receipt, over the policy cap, or included alcohol?
Work out how much we overpaid on each of those claims and in total.
Draft agent instructions for an expense checker that reads a receipt image and the claim, applies the Expenses Policy and returns approve / query with a reason.
success_criteria: All paid claims with issues are found (see answer key).
Overpayment is calculated, with the method shown.
The design keeps a human approver in the loop and explains what the automation must not decide alone.
The agent's flags match the answer key on at least 28 of 31 claims.
agent_instructions: You are the Delcorn expense pre-check assistant. For each claim you are given (claim row and receipt image): 1) read the receipt total, date, merchant and line items; 2) compare the receipt total with the claimed amount; 3) apply the Expenses Policy caps (breakfast £10, lunch £10, evening meal £30) and the no-alcohol rule; 4) check whether the same claimant has already claimed the same merchant, date and amount; 5) return APPROVE or QUERY, the reason, and the maximum payable amount. Never reject a claim yourself - a human approver decides. If the receipt is unreadable, return QUERY with 'receipt unreadable'.
trainer_notes: Expected paid-with-issues claims are in the answer key (exp_paid_with_issues). Overpayment = claimed minus the lower of receipt total and the cap, minus any alcohol.
